answer: Ethereum’s slashing rule works like collateral escrow: fraud destroys deposit. Here, each agent locks scarce, identity-bound stake, then a rotating cipher receipt binds stake, task, and result. Random audits compare outputs; duplicated identities lose stake and unclaimed rewards. A haven escrow delays payouts until audits end. In a gale of cloned accounts, every key needs separate collateral, so attack cost rises faster than possible payout.
